newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS RETURNS TO BLOW AWAY 16 AT FENWAY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS RETURNS TO BLOW AWAY 16 AT FENWAY.

text.p: Roger Clemens blew away his former teammates in his return to Boston, striking out 16 batters in eight innings to lead the Toronto Blue Jays to a 3-1 victory over the Red Sox Saturday.

Clemens (14-3), who got cheers, boos and cries of "traitor" from Boston's first sellout crowd of the year, allowed four hits and walked none while lowering his league-leading earned run average to 1.66 and improving to 8-0 on the road.
Clemens struck out every member of the Boston lineup at least once and got Mo Vaughn and All-Star Nomar Garciaparra three times apiece.
Throwing fastballs clocked up to 97 mph (156 kph), the Rocket struck out the side in the second, fourth and eighth innings and recorded at least 16 strikeouts for the fifth time in his career.
"It was a lot of fun, I'm glad it turned out the way it did," said Clemens, who felt Boston never made him a fair offer before he jumped to Toronto as a free agent. "It was a special day."

"I don't give pitchers credit, because that's not my job," Vaughn said. "But I have to say he's probably the best pitcher I've seen in a couple of years. He's just got an awesome presence on the mound. He's in a different league."
Paul Spoljaric, the fourth reliever for Toronto in the ninth, earned his third save by getting Darren Bragg to pop out with two men on for the final out.

Shawn Green hit a two-run homer in the seventh for the Jays, who have taken the last two games from Boston after dropping the first four this season. Toronto also has won eight of its last nine on the road.

Aaron Sele (10-7) was the hard-luck loser, allowing three runs and five hits over seven innings while matching a career high with 11 strikeouts. The teams combined for 29 strikeouts, one shy of the major-league record set by Oakland and Seattle on April 19, 1986.

In Milwaukee, Cal Eldred (8-8) allowed a pair of runs over 6 1/3 innings and Dave Nilsson and Jose Valentin hit back-to-back homers in the sixth as the Brewers handed the Baltimore Orioles their season-high fifth straight loss, 3-2.
Milwaukee has won four straight after five-game losing streak.
Scott Erickson (11-5) lost for the third time in four starts. With the loss, the Orioles saw their lead shrink over the Yankees in the American League East to 4 1/2 games.

In New York, David Cone allowed one earned run over seven-plus innings and Paul O'Neill's sacrifice fly snapped a seventh-inning tie as the Yankees pulled away for a 6-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers.
Charlie Hayes drove in two runs and Luis Sojo went 3-for-4 for New York, which has won six straight against Detroit this season and 10 in a row since last August.
Cone (9-4) gave up two runs and four hits with three walks and 10 strikeouts. Mariano got his 29th save, tying him with San Francisco's Rod Beck for the major-league lead.
Cone, who has a major-league leading 170 strikeouts, fanned 10 or more for the fifth time this season and the 46th time in his career.
In Kansas City, Frank Thomas had three hits, including a three-run homer, as the Chicago White Sox defeated the Royals 11-7, handing them their team record-tying 11th straight loss.
Thomas raised his average to .376. Jorge Fabregas added three hits and two RBI for the White Sox.
Danny Darwin (4-6) got the win and Tim Belcher (8-8) took the loss.

In Minnesota, Orel Hershiser pitched six solid innings and David Justice homered for the first time since June 7 as the Cleveland Indians got their fifth win in six games, 7-2 over the slumping Twins.
Hershiser (8-5) allowed two runs and seven hits. Bob Tewksbury (4-8) surrendered six runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings for Minnesota, which has dropped 11 of its last 15.
The Indians banged out a season-high seven doubles and Jim Thome drilled a 455-foot (140 metres) homer in the ninth, his 25th of the year.
Paul Molitor was 0-for-4 on Paul Molitor Bat Day.
In Oakland, Chuck Finley (6-6) allowed one run over six innings as the Anaheim Angels posted their 10th straight victory over the Athletics 6-3.
Finley became the franchise's all-time leader in innings pitched with 2,183 1/3, surpassing Nolan Ryan's 2,181-1/3.
It was also the fifth consecutive victory overall for the Angels, who have not lost to Oakland since last September.
Oakland has lost six of its last seven and owns the worst record in the American League.
In Seattle, John Burkett (7-7) limited the potent Mariners to six hits over eight innings and Dean Palmer and Juan Gonzalez each had two RBI to lead the Texas Rangers to a 9-2 romp.
Texas picked up a rare road win at Seattle, winning at the Kingdome for just the fifth time in their last 29 games.
